Early June observations already include peaks of 34.1°C, yet day-to-day variability from thundery showers and sea-breeze effects keeps 30–32°C the most probable range for any single date. Model consensus and historical analogs indicate limited upside beyond 33°C without sustained clear skies, while downside below 30°C remains unlikely given the current seasonal baseline.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent heatwave intensification across southern Pakistan, driven by persistent high-pressure systems and above-normal solar heating, positions 37–38°C as the leading outcomes for Karachi’s June 10 maximum, with market-implied odds of 68% combined. Official Pakistan Meteorological Department guidance and ensemble model runs indicate daytime highs of 35–38°C under clear skies and low wind, consistent with June climatology where the city averages 35–36°C but has seen frequent exceedances this season due to urban heat-island effects and elevated humidity from the Arabian Sea. No significant monsoon moisture or cooling frontal passages are expected before mid-month, keeping probabilities anchored near these thresholds while leaving room for 1–2°C forecast adjustments from updated runs.
